opportunity_map.what_happens_today: Three separately addressed properties (c4), desks staffed around the clock (c12). The published FAQ already codifies the standard answers, check-in 4PM and check-out 11AM (c8), 24 hours cancellation notice (c13), no late check-outs mid-May through mid-September (c7), and that third-party pricing can't be adjusted after the fact (c10).
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_help: A staff-facing retrieval assistant that puts the correct, property-specific and season-specific answer in a clerk's hands in seconds with the source attached. The corpus is unusually good, small, bounded, already public, already permissioned, already in the company's own voice.
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_not: It can't do the welcome. Mews, a PMS vendor surveying its own base, reports 59% of hoteliers say the front desk welcome and check-in should stay human-led (c31), and the company's own hiring language is about caring, personal experiences (c5). Nor should a model ever state a rate or a cancellation outcome to a guest (c30).

opportunity_map.area: Phone paths and the direct-booking line
opportunity_map.what_happens_today: Discounted rates gated behind a single toll-free line (c9). A second named line for extended stay and corporate (c1). A general inbox published under all three properties (c3).
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_help: Triage and routing on the WRITTEN channels, sorting the general inbox (c3) by property and intent. Drafting first-pass written replies for a human to check.
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_not: It can't size this problem, and neither can we. The 40% unanswered-calls figure is a vendor VP statement with no study (c46) and may not size anything. No call volume for this company is published. A voice agent here would answer the one call type where the evidence is worst, rate and cancellation questions (c30).

opportunity_map.what_happens_today: The van runs 24 hours to the airport and rail station (c17), every pickup guest-initiated by phone (c11), excluding tour groups and large groups traveling together (c18). Seasonal Shuttle Bus Drivers are on the roster (c6).
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_help: Structured intake of a free-text arrival message so a guest texts a flight arrival and the desk gets a parsed pickup record. One messy-input node, the only genuinely AI-shaped part.
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_not: The dispatch decision is a rule, not a judgment. The group exclusion (c18) is a stated policy deterministic software can apply and test exhaustively. The desk is already staffed 24/7 (c12), which removes the usual after-hours argument for a voice agent entirely.

opportunity_map.what_happens_today: A five-hour published turn window (c8) and the company's own concession that it can't offer late check-outs in summer (c7). Seasonal Housekeeping and Laundry on the roster (c6).
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_help: Route optimisation is the single best-evidenced AI application in the package. An independent eight-week test measured 2.5 minutes saved per room clean (c36), about EUR 13,800/yr at 80 rooms and 73% occupancy (c37). Housekeeping is the worst departmental shortage at 38% (c34).
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_not: This is a BUY, not a build, and saying so is the honest answer. The same reviewer called the marketed 500% ROI fiction while confirming savings are real (c38, c39). The figure is property-specific and can't be rescaled (c37).

opportunity_map.what_happens_today: The Golden Bear Restaurant is open mid-May to mid-September (c16). Those dates belong to the restaurant and nothing else.
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_help: Almost nothing worth doing. The only real item is that the restaurant's open/closed state is asked constantly and gets wrong in shoulder weeks, so it belongs in the answer set as a dated card.
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_not: No menu, covers, kitchen or F&B data is verified, so any forecasting or menu-engineering pitch would be invented. Out of scope and it stays out.

opportunity_map.what_happens_today: Seasonal Group Representatives are a named hire (c6), and group handling is distinct enough that the van excludes tour groups (c18).
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_help: Drafting structured first-pass replies to inbound group enquiries arriving as free text (c3), with a human filling every number.
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_not: The fact-checker forbade citing the group booking system, the RFP path, the venues or capacities. Anything proposed here would rest on nothing. A real area with no verified surface, it belongs behind a discovery conversation, not in a build.

opportunity_map.what_happens_today: Sold as a separate human-routed path outside the booking engine (c2), routed to one named person whose address is the only email on the homepage (c1).
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_help: First-pass drafting of written enquiry responses, assembling property detail while a human supplies availability and price. Industry analogue is Amadeus Email to RFP (c40).
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_not: It can't quote. The pull-through is a negotiated rate and a relationship, and Amadeus's own first pilot is reported with no baseline and no numbers at all (c41). Enquiry volume is invisible from outside.

opportunity_map.area: The seasonal labour cycle, hiring and onboarding
opportunity_map.what_happens_today: 'We more than double our current hotel staffing for summer' (c5). The roster is the front of house itself, Seasonal Front Desk Clerks plus seven other seasonal titles (c6). AHLA: 65% of 282 hoteliers report shortages (c33), 71% had unfillable openings averaging six to seven per property (c35).
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_help: The highest-leverage area on the map, and the leverage is not recruiting, it is the handover of operating knowledge to people who are new every year.
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_not: It can't recruit, and the funnel is a commodity space where we can't see applicant flow. It can't touch headcount claims, 2018's 170-350 (c23) conflicts with Indeed's 51-200 (c26), so use no headcount at all.

opportunity_map.area: Rate, channel and the direct-booking push
opportunity_map.what_happens_today: Direct booking pushed in capitals (c9), and the FAQ tells guests third-party pricing can't be changed afterwards (c10). Rate ranges published by Explore Fairbanks (c20, c21, c22), DMO listings not company figures.
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_help: In principle a guest-facing assistant shortening the path to direct booking. In practice this is where the evidence most strongly says do not.
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_not: The most rigorous study in the package points straight here. Inaccuracy produced an effect more than four times larger than incredibility (c28), discomfort cut willingness by nearly 38% (c29), and inaccuracy nearly doubled the likelihood of delaying or abandoning a booking, attached specifically to room rates and cancellation policies (c30). A rate-quoting bot is the highest-risk build available and we will not propose one.

opportunity_map.area: The twice-a-year product switch, summer season and aurora season
opportunity_map.what_happens_today: Two different products a year. Wedgewood's Aurora Season Special runs August 21 through April 21 (c14). Bear Lodge's rooms page dates aurora season mid-August to late April with a courtesy Northern Lights wakeup call and rentable headlamps (c19). Bear Lodge calls itself a seasonal hotel with no dates (c15). The Golden Bear's window is mid-May to mid-September (c16). Late check-outs unavailable mid-May through mid-September (c7).
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_help: Season-aware answers. A clerk on August 22 needs a different correct answer than the same clerk on August 20, on late check-out, the restaurant, the wakeup call and headlamps, and that switch lands two weeks after this study's date (c14).
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_not: It can't decide the dates, the company does. Two of their own pages date aurora season differently, August 21 to April 21 (c14) and mid-August to late April (c19). That is a normal artifact of maintaining many pages over many years, NOT a sign of anything wrong, and it is cheap to make canonical. It is concrete proof a single canonical answer has value before any model is involved.

opportunity_map.area: Back office and the general inbox
opportunity_map.what_happens_today: askus@fountainheadhotels.com is the general guest inbox, published under all three properties with no name attached (c3).
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_help: Classification and routing by property and intent, a well-bounded low-cost-of-error task with a human at the far end.
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_not: No back-office, accounting, procurement or compliance surface is verified anywhere. Any pitch about invoices or AP would be invented, and it is excluded.

opportunity_map.area: Brand, independence and the competitive picture
opportunity_map.what_happens_today: Established 1985 (c26). Operations Manager Bobby Hanson described the company in 2018 as 'We're truly local and independent,' (c25). Tim Cerny spoke in April 2026 about twenty years of recognition for what they do in Fairbanks (c27). The Fairbanks Hampton lists Digital Key (c42) and the Fairbanks SpringHill lists Mobile Key (c43). Hilton launched an AI Planner to all hilton.com visitors as of March 17 2026 (c44), Marriott introduced Ask Bonvoy in beta June 16 2026 (c45).
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_help: The competitive read is NOT that this company is behind. Both nearby amenity listings are exactly that, listings, and neither page describes a check-in flow (c42, c43). Ask Bonvoy is a US-English beta to a subset of members (c45). What the brands buy is scale-priced consistency. An independent's counter-position is a human who is always right, a different and cheaper thing to build.
opportunity_map.where_ai_could_not: It shouldn't produce a me-too app. Chasing Digital Key would spend an independent's money to match a chain amenity no verified source ties to a guest outcome, and it would cut against the company's own stated identity (c25).

outcome.statement: A first-week seasonal front-of-house hire gives the same correct, current answer a ten-year veteran would give, at any of the three properties and in either season, without escalating to a supervisor and without a guest ever talking to a machine.
outcome.measurable_as: Four measures, NONE of which exists today, so establishing the baseline is the first two weeks of the work. One, days from a seasonal hire's start to their first unsupervised solo shift. Two, escalations to a supervisor per shift on questions the published answer set already covers (c7, c8, c10, c11, c12, c13, c17, c18, c19). Three, the count of contradictory or stale answers found in a one-time audit across three properties and both seasons, with the aurora-season date difference (c14 versus c19) as the known starting item. Four, no increase in guest complaints tied to policy answers, the guardrail measure, because a build that speeds up wrong answers is worse than nothing.
outcome.why_this_outcome: Stated as a change in staff behaviour, not as a tool, so a deterministic answer is allowed to win it and the AI has to earn its place. It ties to the strongest verified fact in the package (c5) and the roster it hires (c6). It protects rather than replaces what the company says it hires for, which keeps it clear of both evidenced hazards, guest-facing inaccuracy on rates and cancellations (c30) and removing the human from the welcome (c31).

opportunity_scores.opportunity: A first-week seasonal front-of-house hire answers guest questions as correctly as a veteran
opportunity_scores.reasoning: Importance high because the company itself says it more than doubles hotel staffing for summer (c5) and the roster it names is the front of house absorbing guest contact (c6), across three separately located properties (c4). Satisfaction is NOT zero, and saying so matters, they have already codified the standard answers in a public FAQ and staff the desk 24/7 (c12). It sits at 4 because that content is written for guests, spread across marketing pages, and lacks the property and season splits a clerk needs.

opportunity_scores.opportunity: Operating knowledge survives the twice-a-year switch between summer and aurora season
opportunity_scores.reasoning: The business genuinely sells two products with different amenities, policies and guest questions (c19, c16, c7). Satisfaction lowest on the list because no mechanism is visible in any verified source, and two of their own pages date aurora season differently (c14 versus c19). Judgment anchored on cited facts, not measurements.

opportunity_scores.opportunity: Corporate and extended-stay enquiries get a fast, accurate first response
opportunity_scores.reasoning: Sold as its own path outside the booking engine (c2). Satisfaction mid because the company already solved it deliberately with a named manager and a direct line on the homepage (c1). Evidence is thin, one homepage line, and the industry analogue reports no numbers at all (c41).

opportunity_scores.opportunity: More demand books direct rather than through third-party sites
opportunity_scores.reasoning: High on margin grounds and the company shouts about it in capitals (c9). HIGH SCORE, DISQUALIFYING RISK. The only rigorous study measures AI inaccuracy about room rates and cancellation policies nearly doubling booking abandonment (c30). Scores do not get to auto-decide.

opportunity_scores.opportunity: Rooms are turned inside the eleven-to-four window at peak occupancy
opportunity_scores.reasoning: The company's FAQ concedes the summer constraint by removing late check-outs (c7). Satisfaction highest on the list because the policy solution already works. Best evidence points at a product to BUY (c36, c38).

opportunity_scores.opportunity: Guests get into the courtesy van without the desk fielding every arrival by phone
opportunity_scores.reasoning: Touches every arriving guest (c17, c11). Satisfaction mid because the process is published, understood, and backed by a desk staffed around the clock (c12), so there is no unstaffed window to fix. We may not size the call load (c46).

opportunity_scores.opportunity: The seasonal roster gets filled each spring
opportunity_scores.reasoning: Excluded from targeting because recruiting-funnel AI is a commodity space, we can't see applicant flow, and we may not use any headcount figure (c23 conflicts with c26).

target_opportunity.name: One correct, current answer for every guest question, across three properties and two seasons, in the hands of a front-of-house roster that more than doubles every summer
target_opportunity.why: It merges the two highest-scoring opportunities, 14 and 13, which share a single root, the answer set is scattered and the people using it are new. It rests on the strongest verified fact (c5) and the roster it names (c6). Data readiness, which AI_SCOPING calls the hidden project that kills most builds, is unusually good, the corpus already exists, is small, bounded, permissioned and in the company's own voice. The observable inconsistency between the two aurora-season date ranges (c14 versus c19) proves value before a model is involved. It is STAFF-FACING, which sidesteps both evidenced hazards at once (c30, c31). On the Four Forces, push and pull clear anxiety and habit, but only narrowly and only because the build stays behind the desk. HABIT IS THE STRONGEST OPPOSING FORCE, a 24/7 staffed desk (c12) makes asking a veteran genuinely easy, so anything built has to be faster than turning your head.

candidate_builds.name: The Desk Answer Book
candidate_builds.what_it_is: A staff-facing, season-aware, property-aware canonical answer set. Every question a clerk gets becomes one card with one correct answer, a property tag, a date range, a source and a change log. Built from the company's own published content plus their internal SOPs, with deterministic keyword and tag search, a season toggle that flips on the dated boundaries (c14, c16, c19) and a printable shift sheet. NO MODEL ANYWHERE IN IT.
candidate_builds.reach: Every seasonal front-of-house hire at all three properties (c4), across all eight seasonal titles (c6), plus year-round staff. The exact number is not published anywhere we may cite, and counting it is part of the work. Reach index 3 of 3.
candidate_builds.effort: Small. Weeks, not quarters. The content largely exists and the hard part is editorial, agreeing on the one right answer per question.
candidate_builds.rice_note: 3 x 1.5 x 0.9 / 1 = 4.05, THE HIGHEST SCORE IN THIS SET. Confidence 0.9 because we can see the corpus and can point at a concrete defect it fixes (c14 versus c19). This is Google's Rule of ML number one applied honestly.
candidate_builds.cost_of_delay: Moderate and dated. Aurora season begins August 21 (c14), sixteen days after this study's date, and the Golden Bear closes mid-September (c16), so a season-flip is the natural first proving ground. Miss it and the next comparable event is the spring hire-up, roughly eight months out.
candidate_builds.honest_downside: It answers the question you knew how to look up. It does not handle paraphrase, and it does not handle composite questions, the ones that actually stall a new clerk, like a 1am rail arrival for a party of twelve wanting early access, which composes the shuttle instruction (c11), the 24-hour van (c17), the group exclusion (c18) and the 4PM check-in (c8). It also dies the way every binder dies, from unowned maintenance, so an owner has to be named on day one.

candidate_builds.name: Desk Copilot
candidate_builds.what_it_is: A staff-facing retrieval assistant sitting on top of the canonical answer set, reachable from a phone or the desk browser. A clerk types or dictates the guest's actual question and gets an answer in plain language with the source card cited beneath it, plus an explicit 'I don't know, escalate' path. Hard constraints wired in, never guest-facing, never states a rate, never states a cancellation outcome, always shows its source.
candidate_builds.reach: Same as the Answer Book (c4, c6). Reach index 3 of 3.
candidate_builds.effort: Medium. The retrieval layer is small work, the evaluation set and the guardrails are the real work.
candidate_builds.rice_note: 3 x 2.0 x 0.7 / 2 = 2.1. Confidence deliberately held at 0.7 because AI_SCOPING is explicit that nearly every business can build a RAG proof of concept and very few run one reliably in production, and because no evaluation set exists yet. What raises it above a typical RAG punt is that the corpus is small, clean, public and stable, the condition under which retrieval precision holds. Cost of error is low by design, a human reads every answer before a guest hears it.
candidate_builds.cost_of_delay: Same August 21 season flip (c14), plus a larger window at the spring hire-up. Neither is urgent enough to justify skipping the canonical layer first.
candidate_builds.honest_downside: Confident wrong answers are the failure mode, and hospitality has the receipts (c28). It is strictly dependent on the Answer Book existing, pointing retrieval at an uncanonicalized pile of marketing pages would reproduce the aurora-date contradiction with a confident voice attached, which is worse than the contradiction.

candidate_builds.name: Arrival Desk, structured intake and dispatch
candidate_builds.what_it_is: The guest-initiated shuttle call (c11) becomes a structured arrival record. A guest texts a flight or train arrival, one thin AI node parses the free text into terminal, time and party size, and everything after that is deterministic, the group exclusion (c18) applied as a rule, a shared dispatch board (c17), and a driver view.
candidate_builds.reach: Arriving and departing guests only. Reach index 2 of 3.
candidate_builds.effort: Medium to high. Needs an SMS channel, a dispatch surface and a driver device, and it touches a live guest-facing process.
candidate_builds.rice_note: 2 x 2.0 x 0.55 / 3 = 0.73. Confidence penalised hard because we can't size arrival call load and are forbidden from using the only number available (c46). An opportunity we can't size can't be confidently ranked.
candidate_builds.cost_of_delay: Low. The van already runs 24 hours (c17) and the desk is already staffed 24 hours (c12), so nothing degrades by waiting.
candidate_builds.honest_downside: This is the slot where a voice agent would normally get proposed, and it is worth saying plainly why one should not be. The desk is staffed 24/7 BY DESIGN (c12), so there is no unattended window to cover, which is the usual justification. The group exclusion (c18) is a judgment made live with a guest on the phone. It replaces a published process guests already understand, so habit works against it and the win is unmeasurable without a baseline nobody has.

candidate_builds.name: Corporate and Extended-Stay Response Desk
candidate_builds.what_it_is: A drafting assistant on the written enquiries landing on the published homepage address (c1) and the general inbox (c3), assembling a property-specific first response, with availability and price left as blanks a human fills before anything sends. Attacks the REVENUE side rather than the cost side, which is why it is on this list.
candidate_builds.reach: One routing path and effectively one named person (c1). Reach index 1 of 3.
candidate_builds.rice_note: 1 x 2.5 x 0.4 / 2 = 0.5, the LOWEST score despite the highest impact per unit, which is exactly what the Confidence term is for. Evidence is one homepage sentence (c2) and one routing line (c1), and the industry analogue is a vendor press release whose named first pilot is reported with no baseline and no numbers (c40, c41).
candidate_builds.cost_of_delay: Genuinely real and dated. Aurora season opens August 21 (c14), so winter corporate and extended-stay enquiries are landing in that inbox now. The strongest cost-of-delay case on the list and it still does not carry the candidate.
candidate_builds.honest_downside: It points at one person's inbox, so the entire value swings on an enquiry volume nobody outside the company can see. It proposes to sit in front of a human routing choice the company made deliberately and put on its homepage (c1), a hard sell for a forty-year-old independent (c26) that describes itself as truly local and independent (c25).

provisional_pick.name: Desk Copilot, delivered on the Answer Book as a funded phase one
provisional_pick.why_this_one: The honest reading of the RICE table is that the Answer Book wins outright at 4.05, and the pick does not overrule that, it CONTAINS it. Phase one is the Answer Book exactly as scored, and it ships first because it is the data-readiness project AI_SCOPING says is the hidden work behind every RAG build. The gate is explicit, after phase one runs through the August 21 season flip (c14) we measure the residual, how often a clerk still escalates on a question the answer set covers, and how many of those were composite or paraphrased rather than lookups. Only if the residual is real does the copilot layer get funded. That gate has teeth, and the outcome where we build phase one, measure it, and tell them the search box is enough is a GOOD outcome, not a failed engagement. Naming the copilot rather than the Answer Book alone is choosing the higher ceiling, because the escalations that actually cost a new clerk time are the composite ones a keyword search structurally can't serve. This pick stays clear of both evidenced hazards, never guest-facing so it never states a rate or cancellation outcome (c30), and it never touches the welcome (c31).
provisional_pick.why_not_the_others: Not the Answer Book alone, because it is the phase one of this pick rather than a rival, and stopping there by default would leave the composite-question tail unserved without ever measuring whether it matters. Not the Arrival Desk, because the desk is already staffed 24 hours (c12) so there is no unattended window to close, the group exclusion is a live human judgment (c18), and we are forbidden from sizing the call load (c46). It is also where this shop's documented reflex toward voice agents would land, and the evidence argues against one. Not the Corporate Response Desk, despite the best cost-of-delay story and highest per-unit impact, because its evidence base is one homepage sentence (c2), its analogue reports literally no numbers (c41), and its reach is one inbox. Not housekeeping route optimisation, which has the best independent measurement in the package (c36), because that is a product to BUY rather than a thing for us to build, the figure does not travel off its 80 rooms and 73% occupancy (c37), and the reviewer who confirmed the savings called the marketed ROI fiction (c38). Saying buy that one, we won't build it, is the correct answer and it goes in the study. Not a direct-booking assistant, which scored 11, because the most rigorous evidence says AI inaccuracy about rates and cancellation policies nearly doubles booking abandonment (c30).
provisional_pick.what_would_change_my_mind: Four things, in order. One, if the phase one audit finds the answer set is already canonical and consistent across three properties and both seasons, the whole opportunity shrinks and the pick should move to the corporate path. Two, if the residual escalations after phase one are overwhelmingly simple lookups rather than composite questions, we stop at the Answer Book and say so. Three, if Becky Kunkle's enquiry path carries high volume with slow first responses, a fact only they can supply, the Corporate Response Desk becomes competitive. Four, IF THE SEASONAL ROSTER TURNS OUT TO BE SUBSTANTIALLY RETURNING STAFF rather than new hires, the push force weakens badly and the target opportunity drops, since the whole case rests on the roster being new. We have no evidence either way and it is the first question to ask.

what_the_roadmap_should_carry_later: Housekeeping route optimisation as an explicit BUY-DO-NOT-BUILD recommendation, carrying both halves of the independent evidence (c36, c37) and (c38, c39). It attaches to a company-stated constraint (c7, c8) and the worst departmental shortage industry-wide (c34).

The corporate and extended-stay response path (c1, c2, c3), held in Next rather than Later, gated on one measurement only they can make, enquiry volume and current first-response time. Amadeus's Email to RFP is the analogue and its total absence of reported numbers (c40, c41) is the honest framing.

Structured arrival intake for the courtesy van, deterministic first, with the group exclusion as a tested rule (c18) and a shared dispatch board (c17), and an AI parsing node only if free-text arrival messages prove messy. EXPLICITLY NOT a voice agent, because the desk is staffed 24/7 by design (c12).
Routing and classification on the general inbox (c3), low cost of error with a human at the far end, a natural second use of the same canonical answer set.

A named owner and a review cadence for the canonical answer set, tied to the season boundaries the company already publishes (c14, c16, c19). Unowned reference content is the documented way this class of build dies.
A deliberate NON-GOAL to write down and keep, no guest-facing rate or cancellation assistant, with the Texas A&M finding as the stated reason (c28, c29, c30).
A deliberate NON-GOAL on chasing chain app amenities (c42, c43, c45). An independent's counter-position is a human who is always right, not a me-too app.
unknowns_that_matter: How many people the front-of-house roster actually grows by, and what share are RETURNING seasonal staff versus first-time hires. The company says it more than doubles (c5) and does not publish a number. The whole push force of the target opportunity depends on the returning-versus-new split.
Current time-to-competence for a new front desk clerk. No baseline exists anywhere. Collecting it is the first two weeks of the work, and without it there is no honest before-and-after.

Escalation rate per shift on questions the published answer set already covers, and critically the split between simple lookups and composite questions. This single measurement decides whether the copilot layer gets funded or whether the Answer Book is the whole answer.

How many contradictory or stale answers exist across three properties and both seasons. We can see ONE from outside (c14 versus c19). A one-time audit is the only way to know whether that is isolated or a pattern, and we should not assume it is a pattern.
What internal SOP and training material already exists beyond the public pages, in what format, and who owns it. If it is trapped in PDFs or someone's head, that gap IS the project.
Call volume and answer rate on the front desk and toll-free line (c9). Not knowable from outside, and the only industry number available may not size anything here (c46).
Enquiry volume and current first-response time on the extended-stay and corporate path (c1, c2). The one measurement that could promote the runner-up to the pick.
Channel mix between direct and third-party bookings (c9, c10).
What property management, booking and messaging systems are actually in place, and what they expose. Nothing verified names a system, and no integration edge can be promised until they are named.
